subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class core browser-plugin config for per-agent/subagent browser profile binding plus per-profile proxy settings, or should this remain external/CDP/ClawHub-style orchestration?
rationale: The current code proves the requested fields are missing, but adding them changes public config, secrets handling, browser egress, and agent/session ownership semantics; those are product and security decisions rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Design the core browser contract
options.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for per-profile proxy, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, and diagnostics before implementation.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Keep this open but make proxy transport and subagent browser ownership separate maintainer-owned tracks, with this issue as the umbrella reference.

options.title: Defer to external orchestration
options.body: Document Remote CDP, browser-lock-style wrappers, or ClawHub plugins as the supported path and close only after maintainers decide not to add core config.

recommendation.title: Design the core browser contract
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for per-profile proxy, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, and diagnostics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser profile, extension-driver, docs, and security-boundary work makes steipete the strongest routing candidate for the product-direction call.
